prompt:
Document type: adjuster_file. Page 1 of 2.

<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1012
Claimant:
Steven Lindsey
Adjuster:
Chelsea Hebert
January 21, 2025
Claim received for a side impact at an intersection involving the insured's vehicle, with the claimant reporting
whiplash. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will be routed through the attorney's office.
February 6, 2025
Verified that the driver involved is named on the policy and that the coverage was active at the time of loss. Nothing in
the policy records suggests any issue with the timing of coverage.
February 12, 2025
Obtained the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the scene and matches the general
description of the collision given to us.
March 3, 2025
Reviewed the photos submitted by the insured. They confirm the point of impact and several of the reported details,
though no independent witnesses have come forward to add to the account.
March 6, 2025
Vehicle damage appears largely consistent with the side impact as described. The estimator's notes are attached to
the file for reference.
April 3, 2025
A few older scratches were noted on the vehicle. They may predate this collision, and I have asked the appraiser to
separate them from the new damage in the estimate.
April 4, 2025
Claimant's attorney submitted the initial medical summary, which describes whiplash symptoms. The kind and force
of the reported injury line up reasonably well with the crash as described.
May 17, 2025
Reviewed the claimant's prior medical history provided through the attorney. No earlier injury to the same body area
is on record.
June 6, 2025
Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this type of injury. I have requested the treatment notes
to understand the course of care.
June 8, 2025
Claimant later supplied a few additional details about the collision through counsel. The core account has not
cahnged from the original statement.
July 28, 2025
Reviewed the damage estimate against the photos and the described impact. Most of the repair items fit the collision,
and the remaining items are being checked against the older scratches noted earlier.
August 4, 2025
File is pending review of the treatment records and the final repair estimate. No further action is needed until the
medical and repair documentation is complete.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
JSON format:
{"findings": [{"feature": "", "rating": "", "confidence": "", "quote": "", "reason": ""}]}
